indirect_protection_sweep: none found beyond the annotations already visible at the call site — checked: no internal shared library dependency beyond spring-cloud/resilience4j/actuator/sleuth/micrometer (all public, well-known); no @Aspect/@Around/BeanPostProcessor/RestTemplateCustomizer in the codebase; no service mesh manifests present (no istio-manifests/, no linkerd config); this is a single, undecorated Spring Boot application.

boundary.boundary_finding: CRITICAL METHODOLOGICAL RESULT — see summary. This service has no CE, SE, or DI interaction points at all. `HelloService.remoteCall()`, the method wrapped by @TimeLimiter/@Retry/@CircuitBreaker, performs no I/O of any kind: it is `return Mono.just(msg)` after an artificial `delayElement(Duration.ofSeconds(random 0-5))`. There is no HTTP client, no gRPC stub, no database, no external system whose failure this code could ever observe. Per the boundary rule (score only integrations at the frontier whose failure compromises this application's function), this method does not qualify as a CE point — there is no external dependency to be a frontier of. The README's mention of 'keycloak and postgres' is unreflected in any dependency file or code and appears to be a stale artifact from a template this repo was adapted from; verified absent in build.gradle, all .java files, and docker-compose.yml.

mechanisms.name: bulkhead
mechanisms.resolved_value: PRESENT — maxConcurrentCalls=100 (semaphore bulkhead default config); a separate thread-pool-bulkhead config also present (maxThreadPoolSize=4, coreThreadPoolSize=2, queueCapacity=2), though instance-level binding to confirm which bulkhead type backs `sayHello` was not fully resolved from config alone — both configs exist under `resilience4j.bulkhead` defaults
mechanisms.note: This is genuine protection of the service's OWN concurrency/thread-pool exhaustion — real regardless of what the wrapped operation does. Scored on its own merits, independent of the boundary finding above.

set_aside.name: rate limiter configured but never applied
set_aside.evidence: application.yml declares resilience4j.ratelimiter.configs.default (limitForPeriod=10, limitRefreshPeriod=1s) in full, but no @RateLimiter annotation exists anywhere in the codebase — the configuration block is orphaned.
set_aside.note: Distinct from UNVERIFIED (where a mechanism is referenced but its value can't be resolved). This is CONFIGURED-BUT-UNAPPLIED: full calibration exists for a mechanism that protects nothing. Recommended as a distinct status category for MS-1.2 tooling, since it is more informative than silence to a reader auditing their own config for dead entries.

mechanisms.name: readiness_probe
mechanisms.resolution_path: Actuator health endpoint auto-registers CircuitBreaker and RateLimiter health indicators (management.health.circuitbreakers.enabled: true, ratelimiters.enabled: true) — genuinely richer health signal content than any other service audited in this corpus so far. BUT docker-compose.yml defines a `healthcheck` block for prometheus and grafana, and explicitly NOT for the circuitbreaker-demo service itself.
mechanisms.evidence: application.yml:5-6 (health indicator config); docker/docker-compose.yml (circuitbreaker-demo service block, no healthcheck key, contrast with prometheus/grafana blocks which have one)

mechanisms.name: graceful_shutdown
mechanisms.resolution_path: Spring Boot 2.4.4 supports server.shutdown=graceful (available since 2.3), but no such key found in application.yml

mechanisms.name: declared_resource_limits
mechanisms.resolution_path: docker-compose.yml circuitbreaker-demo service has no deploy.resources block at all

totals.domains_rationale: Single domain — a greeting endpoint pattern showcase. Only EE (5) and AC (18) verticals have a present instance; CE/SE/DI are correctly excluded from index_max, not scored as 0/15 etc., because no interaction point of those kinds exists in this topology.

remediation.action: Wire the existing Actuator health endpoint (already rich, with circuit breaker/rate limiter state) to a docker-compose healthcheck
remediation.rationale: The health signal content is better than average in this corpus; it's simply not connected to anything that acts on it — cheapest, highest-value fix available.
